kitchenEType.title: Kitchen equipment type
kitchenEType.additionalInfo: Hood – the air is taken directly from the hood installed above the stove (air exhaust rate of 360 m3/hr).
kitchenEType.span1: Wall type – the extractor is built directly into the wall (this type of equitpemnt has air exhaust rate of 180 m3/hr).

damper.title: Is a damper installation necessary?
damper.additionalInfo: There are two types of connecting the apartment’s air duct to the central ventilation shaft: with a damper and without a damper.
damper.describtion: In multi-apartment buildings, air ducts are one of the main routes for the spread of fire and smoke. Properly connected ventilation slows down the spread of smoke and fire.
damper.span1: When connected with a damper, the horizontal air duct from the apartment has a damper installed and connects to the vertical shaft.
damper.DamperFunctions: In case of fire, the damper closes, reducing the likelihood of odors, smoke, or fire returning to the apartment from the shaft.
damper.WithoutDamperFunctions: With a connection without a damper, the horizontal air duct does not connect directly to the shaft. Instead, the duct first goes vertically upwards and then connects to the exhaust duct.
damper.goal: This type of connection minimizes the risk of smoke spreading to other apartments.
damper.conclusion: As shown in the diagram, with a damper connection, the shaft is smaller, but each kitchen and wet area has an individual damper (the estimated cost of one damper is $150).

shaftVentT.title: Shaft ventilation type
shaftVentT.additionalInfo: In natural ventilation, air moves passively through the duct; the speed is low (2 m/s), and the shaft size is relatively large.
shaftVentT.describtion: In mechanical ventilation, an additional exhaust fan placed on the roof helps the airflow, increasing the speed (6 m/s) and reducing the shaft size.
